newsitem.title: FRANCE: French coalition deputies snub Juppe in march.
newsitem.headline: French coalition deputies snub Juppe in march.

text.p: French Prime Minister Alain Juppe's authority has slipped so far that even parliamentarians from his ruling centre-right coalition are taking to the streets.

About 30 of the parliamentarians walked about one km (600 yards) through light snow to Juppe's office from the National Assembly to present him with a 64-page list of 40 proposals to improve family policy.

"This is to spur the government," said Emile Pinte, a member of Juppe's conservative Rally for the Republic (RPR) party, saying that Juppe had yet to implement some of President Jacques Chirac's 1995 campaign promises on financing education.

Pinte said the march was not intended as criticism of Juppe even though it matched the style of an anti-government rally. Juppe has faced increased sniping from coalition members seeking to distance themselves from the government's unpopular policies.
The deputies' proposals include plans to increase family allowances, introduce a month of paternity leave for fathers of new-borns and step up aid for education.
After meeting Juppe, Pinte said Juppe agreed to ask Labour Minister Jacques Barrot to study the proposals. Opinion polls show Juppe is the least popular prime minister in recent French history.
